text: Log4Shell: remote code execution vulnerability in the Apache Log4j logging library via unsafe JNDI lookups triggered by attacker-controlled input strings, allowing arbitrary code execution on the affected server.
A follow-up flaw to Log4Shell in Apache Log4j: the initial fix was incomplete in certain non-default configurations, still permitting remote code execution or denial-of-service in some deployments.
EternalBlue: remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft SMBv1 server due to improper handling of crafted packets, widely exploited by the WannaCry and NotPetya ransomware worms.
Heartbleed: out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the OpenSSL TLS heartbeat extension, allowing attackers to read sensitive memory contents including private keys and session data from the server.
PrintNightmare: remote code execution and privilege escalation vulnerability in the Windows Print Spooler service, exploitable via crafted print driver installation requests.
BlueKeep: remote code execution vulnerability in Windows Remote Desktop Services (RDP) that does not require authentication, allowing wormable exploitation across a network.
Shellshock: vulnerability in the GNU Bash shell allowing arbitrary command execution via specially crafted environment variables, widely exploitable through CGI web scripts and DHCP clients.
Remote code execution vulnerability in the Apache Struts2 Jakarta Multipart parser via a crafted Content-Type header, notably exploited in the 2017 Equifax data breach.
Zerologon: privilege escalation vulnerability in the Windows Netlogon protocol allowing an attacker to impersonate a domain controller and take over an entire Active Directory domain.

ProxyLogon: server-side request forgery vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Server allowing an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and access mailbox data, often chained with further flaws for remote code execution.
Follina: remote code execution vulnerability in the Microsoft Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT), exploitable via a malicious Office document that does not require macros to be enabled.
Baron Samedit: heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in Sudo allowing any local user to gain root privileges on Unix-like systems, without requiring authentication.
Path traversal vulnerability in Citrix Application Delivery Controller (ADC) and Gateway allowing unauthenticated remote code execution, widely exploited shortly after disclosure.

CurveBall: spoofing vulnerability in the Windows CryptoAPI's validation of Elliptic Curve Cryptography certificates, allowing an attacker to sign malicious code or intercept TLS connections as if trusted.
Dirty COW: race condition in the Linux kernel's memory subsystem allowing a local unprivileged user to gain write access to read-only memory mappings, leading to privilege escalation.
Path traversal vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS SSL VPN web portal allowing an unauthenticated attacker to read system files, including session credentials, from the device.
Remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft MSHTML, exploitable via a malicious ActiveX control embedded in an Office document.

Privilege escalation vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook allowing an attacker to leak a user's NTLM authentication hash by sending a specially crafted email, without requiring the user to open or preview it.
Memory corruption vulnerability in the Microsoft Office Equation Editor component allowing remote code execution via a crafted document, widely used in phishing campaigns for years after disclosure.
SMBGhost: remote code execution vulnerability in the Microsoft SMBv3 protocol's compression handling, allowing wormable exploitation similar to EternalBlue.
